Rescue workers carry Alberto Gil after he was pulled from the rubble a week after he was trapped by twin earthquakes that struck Catia La Mar, Venezuela. in Catia La Mar, Venezuela, Thursday, July 2, 2026. Credit: AP/Fernando Vergara CATIA LA MAR, Venezuela — Rescuers pulled a 43-year-old security guard alive from a collapsed basement early Thursday, ending a grueling days-long operation that became a symbol of hope after the devastation of twin earthquakes that struck Venezuela eight days earlier. Hernán Alberto Gil Flores was extracted safely after being trapped since June 24 under the rubble in the basement of the Galerías Playa Grande shopping center in the coastal town in La Guaira. Rescuers initially made contact with him over the weekend.

Watch: Man rescued from rubble eight days after Venezuela earthquake A man has been rescued alive after being trapped for eight days in the rubble of a building that collapsed after twin earthquakes in Venezuela. Emergency workers managed to free Hernán Gil more than 100 hours after they had first located him under 140 tonnes of rubble. A Chilean firefighter had earlier described the rescue operation as "without doubt the most complex and technically difficult which I've had to tackle". Almost 2,300 people are confirmed to have died in the quakes which hit Venezuela on 24 June, and tens of thousands are still missing. Hundreds of rescue workers from seven countries helped free Hernán Gil Hundreds of rescuers had been working against the clock to free Gil since he was found on Saturday.

Watch: Man rescued from rubble eight days after Venezuela earthquake

A man has been rescued alive after being trapped for eight days in the rubble of a building that collapsed after twin earthquakes in Venezuela.

Emergency workers managed to free Hernán Gil more than 100 hours after they had first located him under 140 tonnes of rubble.

A Chilean firefighter had earlier described the rescue operation as "without doubt the most complex and technically difficult which I've had to tackle".

Almost 2,300 people are confirmed to have died in the quakes which hit Venezuela on 24 June, and tens of thousands are still missing.

Hundreds of rescue workers from seven countries helped free Hernán Gil

Hundreds of rescuers had been working against the clock to free Gil since he was found on Saturday.

Teams from Venezuela, Chile, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Mexico, Portugal and the United States helped to free him.

Parts of the access ducts rescuers built to reach him collapsed several times, highlighting the dangers the work poses to the rescuers as well as Gil.

Overnight, the search teams were finally able to establish visual contact with Gil.

In footage recorded by a small camera inserted into the rubble where Gil was trapped, a Chilean firefighter could be heard asking Gil to turn his head towards the camera.

One of his eyes was bloodshot and he was wearing a face mask, which rescuers had earlier passed to him through a small hole to protect him from the dust and debris created by their efforts to free him.

The firefighter also asked him to don goggles to protect his eyes as rescuers continue to carefully dig away at the rubble surrounding him.

International rescuers monitor man trapped under the rubble

Ricardo Arias from the Costa Rican Red Cross told local journalist Joan Camargo, external that Gil was in a stable condition.

He added that they had been able to give him water and attach him to an intravenous drip.

payload.title: Maanjäristyksessä loukkuun jäänyt mies pelastettiin elossa kahdeksan päivän jälkeen Venezuelassa
payload.summary: Pelastustyöntekijät saivat Hernán Alberto Gil Floresin elossa ulos sortuneen rakennuksen raunioista Venezuelassa kahdeksan päivää maanjäristysten jälkeen. Lähes 2 300 ihmisen on vahvistettu kuolleen ja kymmenettuhansia on yhä kateissa.
payload.content:
Hernán Alberto Gil Flores on pelastettu elossa Venezuelassa kahdeksan päivää sen jälkeen, kun kaksi maanjäristystä romahdutti rakennuksia Catia La Marin alueella. 43-vuotias vartija oli jäänyt loukkuun Galerías Playa Grande -ostoskeskuksen kellarikerroksen raunioihin La Guairan rannikkokaupungissa 24. kesäkuuta iskeneiden järistysten jälkeen.

## Pelastus kesti päiviä

Pelastajat saivat Gilin ulos varhain torstaina 2. heinäkuuta Catia La Marissa. Häneen oli saatu yhteys jo viikonloppuna, minkä jälkeen satojen pelastajien työ jatkui tunti tunnilta vaikeissa oloissa. Operaatiota seurattiin laajasti, koska eloonjääneen löytyminen raunioista toi toivoa tuhojen keskelle.

Gilin kerrotaan olleen noin 140 tonnin raunioiden alla. Pelastustyöntekijät onnistuivat vapauttamaan hänet yli 100 tuntia sen jälkeen, kun hänet oli ensin paikannettu. Lähdetietojen mukaan hän myös rohkaisi pelastajia, kun nämä etenivät hitaasti kohti häntä sortuneen monikerroksisen pysäköintirakennuksen ja ostoskeskuksen raunioissa.

Chilestä tullut palomies kuvasi operaatiota poikkeuksellisen monimutkaiseksi ja teknisesti vaikeaksi. Pelastustöihin osallistui ryhmiä Venezuelasta, Chilestä, Costa Ricasta, El Salvadorista, Meksikosta, Portugalista ja Yhdysvalloista. Kansainvälinen apu oli mukana työssä, jota tehtiin sortuneen rakennuksen kellaritiloissa raskaiden raunioiden keskellä.

## Tuhansia kuolleita

Gilin pelastuminen tapahtui keskellä laajaa tuhoa. Lähdetietojen mukaan lähes 2 300 ihmisen on vahvistettu kuolleen 24. kesäkuuta iskeneissä maanjäristyksissä. Lisäksi kymmenettuhannet ihmiset ovat edelleen kateissa, ja pelastustyöt jatkuivat monilla alueilla.

Catia La Marin rannikkokaupungissa pelastustyöntekijät olivat työskennelleet Gilin löytämisestä lähtien aikaa vastaan, jotta hänet saataisiin turvallisesti ulos. Hänen pelastamisensa kahdeksan päivän jälkeen on poikkeuksellinen selviytyminen katastrofissa, jonka kokonaisvaikutukset ovat Venezuelassa edelleen raskaat.
